key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled finite element solver combines near-wall and bulk transport models to enable inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with agentic AI optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets high-Péclet transport problems, reducing mesh demands while preserving governing equations, boundary conditions, and interface continuity during parameter inference.
method: Split near-wall and bulk dynamics into overlapping, perturbation-based FEM subproblems.
Differentiate the coupled solver to compute adjoint sensitivities for inverse optimization.
Use LLM-directed updates or an AI agent that stages optimization and expands a functional basis under a prescribed admission policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Agentic optimization benefits may depend on the unknown-field representation and the policy governing candidate basis admission.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
